title: W11 pin never asserts drops land on the shared uplink bundle — a drop set entirely on the wide host bundle (or NO_BUNDLE pool drops) passes vacuously
evidence:
testing.expectf(t, !s.replay_error, "no draw may be rejected (the fixture must be fully wired — a rejected draw would make the pin vacuous")
	testing.expectf(t, drops > 0, "the shared uplink must congest (the aggregation choke is real), got 0 drops")
	testing.expectf(t, narrow_drops == 0,
		"%d drops targeted a narrow access bundle (want 0 — a subscriber's own traffic never congests its drop; congestion lives at the shared uplink)", narrow_drops)
detail: Assertions check drops>0 anywhere and zero on narrow bundles, but no assertion pins drops to pipe 13's bundle. by_bundle keys for the wide host-drop bundle (pipe 12) or NO_BUNDLE (E22) satisfy every assertion without the shared link congesting.
recommended_fix: After the narrow_drops check, assert the shared uplink bundle sheds: resolve b13, ok := bundle_of_pipe(&s, 13) and expectf(t, ok && by_bundle[b13] > 0, ...).

title: test_narrow_access_headroom reads the hand-built mirror, not data/pipe_tiers.json — the claimed 'future retune' protection has an unguarded data-only-retune path
detail: The pin's capacity comes from test_catalog (determinism_test.odin:42), a hand-maintained mirror with no sync test against data/pipe_tiers.json (TEST_CATALOG_HASH is the dummy 0x0123456789ABCDEF). A data-only retune to e.g. 6 u/s leaves this pin green on stale mirror values.
recommended_fix: Add a mirror-sync test loading data/*.json via catalogs_load and comparing tier/balance fields against test_catalog, so data retunes flow into this pin or fail loudly.

title: headroom pin divides by cap_u_s with no zero guard — a zero throughput/cap_fraction operand crashes instead of failing the band check
evidence:
cap_u_s := i64(cat.balance.cap_fraction_permille) * i64(cat.node_types[res_idx].throughput_units) // × 1/1000 u/s (= 2500 = 2.5 u/s)
	headroom_permille := i64(cat.pipe_tiers[narrow].capacity_units) * 1_000_000 / cap_u_s — and core/catalog.odin:361 nt.throughput_units = jint(eo, "throughput_units", 0) (no >0 load rule)
detail: Terminal throughput_units loads with default 0 and has no fail-fast rule (only cap_fraction_permille 1..1000 is validated, and only for catalogs_load — the mirror bypasses load). Zeroing either operand divides by zero: test crash, not a clean band failure.
recommended_fix: Guard before dividing: testing.expectf(t, cap_u_s > 0, "residential cap_u_s must be > 0 (cap_fraction × throughput)") or guard in the test.

title: routing_cost_test stale '5+40' arithmetic in comments and the failure message — live mixed-tier sum is now 10+40=50
detail: The assertion reads live catalog values (passes at 50), but the diff's narrow 5→10 made the stated arithmetic false at lines 233, 291 and in the 295 failure string — a future failure prints a wrong expected number.
recommended_fix: Update the three '5+40'/'narrow 5' strings in routing_cost_test.odin (lines 233, 291, 295) to the 10+40 arithmetic, or derive the message from the catalog values.

title: catalog.odin cap_fraction comment still claims '~2× access headroom' — post-5.10 narrow access is 4× over the 2.5 u/s source cap
evidence: // sources ≤ 0.083 pkts/tick = 2.5 u/s (half its 5 u/s, ~2× access headroom),
detail: This comment documents the cap_fraction tuning rationale next to the field; the 5→10 rebalance makes the headroom claim stale (2.5 u/s vs 10 u/s = 4×). A future retune against the stated ratio would undershoot the card's band.
recommended_fix: Update the catalog.odin:190 comment to '~4× access headroom at the 5.10 narrow tier (10 u/s)' so the tuning rationale matches the data.
